text:
alex: Heads-up — quick triage on weird host decode latency for streaming v2. Tail (95->99th) jumped ~40ms around 14:28 UTC.

maria: I saw that too. Spike aligns with increased small-request traffic. Any recent gateway changes?

jamal: I sampled a few traces. Host-side tokenization + request parsing account for most of the extra time. Roughly tokenize_host ~18ms, parse/chunk-assembly ~12ms per request in the bad traces.

sven: Can you paste the perf dump you used?

jamal: Sure — quick perf aggregate from a 200-sample window:
```
parse_stream_chunks 30%
tokenize_host_utf8_view 25%
grpc_read_loop 10%
http_keepalive_parse 8%
kv_cache_lookup 8%
batch_dispatch 7%
other 12%
```

maria: Noting that kv cache misses increased from ~2% to ~7% in that interval. Could be unrelated but worth watching.

alex: @perf-bot do we have collated flamegraphs for that window?

perf-bot: Collated traces uploaded: https://perf.internal/fg/1785123456 (flamegraph + raw stacks).

sven: We did a kernel-selection heuristic tweak two days ago that changes on-device kernel for long-sequence tails. That shouldn't affect host parse cost directly, but it could change sequence length distribution which then affects batching and host overhead.

jamal: Also found gateway PR #412 reduced streaming chunk size to 4k -> increases number of chunks per request. That raises parse and assembly work on host and pushes more small batches downstream.

maria: So two vectors: batching heuristics + chunk-size change. Either could explain the tail. I can quickly revert the chunk-size tweak in canary and re-run perf.

alex: Good plan. Immediate: rollback gateway chunking change on canary and A/B test. Medium: instrument tokenization path for zero-copy and add microbench for http vs grpc parsing. Assign @katie to run the synthetic test matrix.

katie: On it. I'll run 1k streaming requests each for: HTTP/1 keepalive, HTTP/1 new-conns, gRPC keepalive. Measuring end-to-end, host parse, tokenization, and kv hit/miss for each. Expect results in ~45m.

sven: Also add a tiny KV-sampler in runtime to log hits for the same request IDs so we can correlate parse time vs kv misses. If parse dominates, we should move some chunk-assembly work into the worker thread or use a smaller parse state machine.

jamal: Found a micro-alloc/memcopy in tokenizer when input >8k bytes (we create a contiguous buffer). I can try a zero-copy view to cut ~10-15ms for those cases.

alex: Excellent. For now: 1) rollback gateway chunking on canary 2) Katie runs synthetic matrix 3) Jamal prototypes zero-copy tokenizer 4) Sven adds KV sampler + perf-bot aggregation. If rollback reduces tail, we'll keep it rolled and schedule tokenizer change in a patch release.

maria: I'll draft a small rollback playbook for gateway PR #412 so oncall can do it fast.

perf-bot: CI/deploy update: gateway PR #412 deployed to canary at 2026-03-18T14:15Z (flag: streaming-chunk-size=4k).

alex: Thanks all. Keep updates here — short notes, timestamps, and a link to the perf artifact.

maria: Will update in ~30m with rollback result. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary revert triggered by maria at 2026-03-18T14:46Z — rolling back streaming-chunk-size to 8k on canary.

jamal: After revert, quick re-check shows 95th down ~28ms vs canary with 4k. Still ~12ms above baseline but much better. Need tokenizer patch to close remaining gap.

alex: Nice. Schedule tokenizer fix for tomorrow's sprint and put a regression test in the perf harness for streaming chunk shapes.

katie: Uploading raw synthetic results: https://perf.internal/results/1785123456-synth (http/grpc matrix + CSV timings).
